questions.q: Which component of a computer system is primarily responsible for executing instructions and performing logical calculations?
questions.explanation: CPU executes instructions; the Jul-Oct 2026 W0 submission screen in the solve video shows 'Accepted answer is C. Central Processing Unit (CPU)'.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of an IP address in a computer network?
options: To identify the physical location of the user
To uniquely identify a device connected to a network
To provide power to network interfaces
questions.explanation: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the function of Random Access Memory (RAM)?
options: It permanently stores the operating system.
It acts as volatile, temporary storage for data actively being used.
It handles long-term archival of documents.
It connects the computer to a local network.
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile working memory for data in active use.

questions.q: Which service is responsible for translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses?
questions.explanation: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.

questions.q: A network that connects computers and devices within a limited physical area, such as a single office building or a university laboratory, is known as a:
questions.explanation: A network within a building/lab is a LAN.

questions.q: In the context of a basic computing architecture, which of the following acts as an input device (analogous to a sensor in an IoT system)?
questions.explanation: Keyboard is the input device among the options.

questions.q: A Media Access Control (MAC) address is a hardware identification number typically hardcoded into which component?
questions.explanation: MAC address is burned into the NIC.

questions.q: At the most fundamental hardware level, how is all digital data represented inside a computer?
questions.explanation: Digital data is represented as binary 0s and 1s.

questions.q: Which networking device operates by examining incoming data packets and determining the best path to forward them to their destination across different networks?
questions.explanation: Routers choose paths between different networks.

questions.q: What does the term "Cloud Storage" fundamentally refer to in basic internet architecture?
options: Storing data on a localized external hard drive attached to a router
Storing data on remote servers managed by a provider and accessed via the internet
Compacting and zipping files to save space on a hard drive
Temporarily saving data in the computer's RAM
questions.explanation: Cloud storage = data on provider-managed remote servers accessed over the internet.

questions.q: What is the primary function of an Operating System (OS)?
options: To protect the computer from physical hardware theft
To manage computer hardware resources and provide common services for computer programs
To translate foreign languages on web pages
To physically cool the CPU during heavy workloads
questions.explanation: OS manages hardware resources and provides common services to programs.

questions.q: In a web browser's URL bar, what does the "S" in HTTPS signify?
questions.explanation: HTTPS = HTTP Secure.

questions.q: Before a real-world physical metric (like temperature) can be processed by a computer, an analog signal must usually pass through which component?
questions.explanation: Analog sensor signals pass through an ADC before digital processing.

questions.q: What does the acronym URL stand for?
questions.explanation: URL = Uniform Resource Locator.

questions.q: Which protocol is the foundational standard for transmitting web pages and data over the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation: HTTP is the web's transfer protocol; the 2026 W0 submission screen shows 'Accepted answer is D. Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP)'.

questions.q: Which sensor can detect gases like LPG, CH4, and CO?
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation) shows a 'gas sensor for detecting LPG gas, methane, carbon monoxide'; MQ-5 is that LPG/CH4/CO module (DHT22 temp/humidity, HC-SR04 ultrasonic, PIR motion).

questions.q: Which modulation scheme does Zigbee use for the 2.4 GHz band?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): 'the 2.4 gigahertz band uses OQPSK'.

questions.q: What does the Constrained RESTful Environments (CoRE) framework include for service discovery?
options: REST based protocols such as HTTP and CoAP
questions.explanation: Lecture 04 (IoT Networking Part I): CoRE service discovery uses the resource directory, the registration interface and REST-based protocols (HTTP/CoAP).

questions.q: What is the maximum data rate of Z-Wave communication technology?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): Z-wave 'data rate is up to offered is up to about 100 kbps' over ~30 m.

questions.q: Which protocol is CoAP based on?
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): CoAP 'works on top of UDP in the transport layer'.

questions.q: Which coding scheme is used by the IEEE 802.15.4 standard for transmitting information?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): 'DSSS, the direct sequence spread spectrum coding scheme that is used to transmit information'.

questions.q: What does 'Range' indicate in a sensor?
options: The smallest change in input that can be detected
The difference between the standard value and the value produced by the sensor
The highest and the lowest value of the physical quantity within which the sensor can actually sense
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): range 'means the range of operation lowest value to highest value'.

questions.q: Which organization has developed the ISA 100.11a standard?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): ISA 100.11a 'was developed by international society for automation the ISA'.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the drawbacks of proprietary non-IP-based solutions?
questions.explanation: Lecture 04 (IoT Networking Part I): drawbacks of non-IP solutions: limited flexibility to end users, interoperability, limited last mile connectivity.

questions.q: Which MQTT QoS Level is also known as "at most once" delivery?
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): 'QoS 0 which is about ensuring at most once delivery'.

questions.q: Fill in the blank space designated by the question mark. [Diagram: Input Signal -> Sensor -> ?
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): 'this sensor plus the processor ... this is a transducer. Similarly, actuator plus processor is also a transducer'.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a vector sensor?
options: Its response depends only on the temperature.
Its response depends only on the magnitude of the input.
Its response depends on the magnitude, direction, and orientation of the input parameter.
Its response is independent of the input parameter.
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): vector sensor response depends on 'the magnitude, the direction and the orientation'.

questions.q: Which of the following frequency ranges is used by 6LoWPAN worldwide?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): 6LoWPAN uses '2400 to 2483.5 megahertz frequency band which is used worldwide' (902-929 MHz is North America).

questions.q: In DDS RTPS, data is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): DDS RTPS 'is a data centric binary protocol and this data in this context are termed as topics'.

questions.q: Which of the following IoT protocols is based on the session layer of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: Corrected after checking the lecture (was: MQTT). Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): the only protocol the lecture calls a session protocol is CoAP: 'CoAP is kind of an application layered protocol ... even more specifically it ensures session, so, session protocol' (Misra's slide: 'CoAP - session layer protocol designed by IETF CoRE'). MQTT/AMQP are described only as pub/sub over TCP; uploaders split AMQP vs MQTT, so moderate confidence.

questions.q: What is a significant characteristic of new materials in the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution?
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): 'Newer materials, lighter materials, stronger materials, materials that are recyclable'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Fourth Industrial Revolution?
options: Extensive use of the ubiquitous and mobile internet
Use of artificial intelligence and machine learning
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): steam engine belongs to the first revolution (1760-1840).

questions.q: What is considered the main nervous system of any manufacturing industry?
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): ICT is the backbone/nervous system of manufacturing industries.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a sustainable industry?
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): sustainable industry = energy efficiency, resource conservation, low waste - not reliance on subsidy.

questions.q: What does L, D and T stand for under 'People Engagement' in the Lean production System?
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): people engagement objectives 'learn, do, teach'.

questions.q: Which resource is associated with the 'Optimization' categorization of Smart and connected products?
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): optimization uses optimization solutions/algorithms.

questions.q: State True or False. The amalgamation of CPS and the evolution of Internet-based technologies led to the development of the Industrial Internet.
questions.explanation: Same statement as Jul-Oct 2024 W2 Q14; Industrial Internet = CPS combined with Internet technologies - True.

questions.q: State True or False. Real-time supply chain monitoring reduces inventory and capital requirements.
questions.explanation: Same statement as Jul-Oct 2024 W2 Q15; real-time supply-chain monitoring reduces inventory and capital - True.

questions.q: In the context of Industry 4.0, what is the full form of CPS?
questions.explanation: CPS = Cyber Physical Systems (named in Lecture 06 and Lecture 11).

questions.q: What does ERP stand for in the context of ICT?
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): ICT enables 'Enterprise Resource Planning ERP based systems'.

questions.q: What is a 'value stream' in Lean Production System?
options: A set of tools for production
All the actions required for a product from order to delivery
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): 'value streams are all the actions that are required for a product from order ... to the delivery'.

questions.q: Which of the following are key attributes of a smart business model?
options: Manual processes, cost reduction, and labor dependency
Value proposition, revenue streams, and technologies
Traditional marketing, fixed costs, and limited innovation
Centralized control, non-digital strategies, and fixed processes
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): key attributes are value proposition, revenue stream and technologies.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a component of a Smart Factory?
questions.explanation: Lecture 10 (Smart Factories): smart factory components are smart machines, processes, engineering, devices, IT, analytics - not physical ledgers.

questions.q: In which format is healthcare data transmitted to maintain data uniformity and interoperability?
questions.explanation: Not in Weeks 1-2 transcripts; HL7 (Health Level Seven) is the healthcare data interchange standard (covered in the IIoT healthcare lecture).

questions.q: What are the key characteristics of agility?
questions.explanation: Lecture 10 (Smart Factories): agility covers flexibility, adaptation and self-configuration.

questions.q: What does "reactive computation" in CPS signify?
options: Interaction with the environment in an ongoing manner
questions.explanation: L11: 'reactive computation means ... interaction of the system with the environment in a continuous fashion'.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. In healthcare applications, CPS is used for _____.
questions.explanation: L11: 'robotic surgery or image-guided surgery. These are examples of cyber physical systems ... in healthcare'.

questions.q: Which level in the "5C Architecture" ensures the gathering of precise status information of machines?
questions.explanation: Connection is not offered; in the 5C model the Cyber level is the central hub where information from every machine is gathered to give insight into each machine's status (L11: data 'received at some kind of a hub').

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. Intelligent sensors are capable of _____.
options: Processing sensed data and managing external sensors/devices
questions.explanation: L11: intelligent sensors 'are capable of processing sensed data ... capable of managing and controlling external sensors and devices'.

questions.q: How many steps are there in the PLM solution approach in Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: L12: 'for Industry 4.0, these are the 10 step approaches that can be used for PLM'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a key component of an AR Device?
questions.explanation: L13: AR device components are 'sensors and cameras, projection screen, processing unit, reflection systems like mirrors'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a challenge of AI in IIoT?
questions.explanation: L14 AI: 'challenges of AI in IIoT. Connecting different devices, understanding the data, training the data, making it accessible, making ... actionable'. Lack of data is not listed; connecting devices is.

questions.q: Which of the following is not one of the primary constraints of mobile CPS?
questions.explanation: Not in the transcripts; mobile CPS are constrained by network stability, power and security; design aesthetics is not a constraint.

questions.q: What are the components of the 5C architecture for CPS?
questions.explanation: L11: 5C = connection, conversion, cyber, cognition, configuration.

questions.q: What is one of the key features of CPS in terms of computation?
questions.explanation: L11: 'Reactive computation is very important'.

questions.q: What is a collaboration platform in the context of Industry 4.0?
options: A type of business software that combines organizational networking capacities with operations
A social media platform for employees
questions.explanation: L12 describes a business software platform combining a social/networking layer with business operations, matching option A.

questions.q: What is a key feature of Augmented Reality (AR)?
options: Enhancing the present perception of reality
questions.explanation: L13: AR gives an 'amplified environment, where the present perception of reality is improved'.

questions.q: Who proposed the first use of the phrase "Artificial Intelligence"?
questions.explanation: Not in the transcript; John McCarthy coined the term 'Artificial Intelligence' (1955-56 Dartmouth proposal).

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
options: A program without AI uses a large knowledge base and a heuristic search method
A program with AI uses a large database and an algorithmic search method
A program with AI uses a large knowledge base and a heuristic search method
A program without AI uses a large database and a heuristic search method
questions.explanation: L14: program with AI uses large knowledge base and heuristic search.

questions.q: Which of the following are constraints of mobile CPS?
questions.explanation: Not in the transcripts; network stability, power requirement and security are all standard mobile-CPS constraints.

questions.q: What does Application Security aim to protect against?
questions.explanation: L16: application security protects applications from outsider threats.

questions.q: What is Ransomware?
options: A type of malware that provides a facility to the attacker to lock users' computer files by using encryption and demand money to unlock them
A program that increases computer performance
A system to enhance network speed
A method to secure data from unauthorized access
questions.explanation: L16: ransomware 'provides a facility to the attacker in which the attacker locks the user's computer files by using an encryption and ... demand some money'.

questions.q: What is a major challenge in the deployment of IIoT?
questions.explanation: L17: challenges include cyber security, lack of standardization and legacy installations.

questions.q: What are the three waves of industrial level innovation according to GE?
options: The Internet Revolution, The Digital Revolution, The Industrial Internet
The Industrial Revolution, The Internet Revolution, The Industrial Internet
The Agricultural Revolution, The Internet Revolution, The Industrial Internet
The Scientific Revolution, The Industrial Revolution, The Internet Revolution
questions.explanation: L18: 'first wave was the industrial revolution ... second wave was the internet revolution ... third wave ... industrial internet'.

questions.q: What is a major drawback of the Industrial Revolution?
options: It had no impact on the environment
It created a bad working environment and inefficient processes
It reduced the use of fossil fuels
It enhanced the quality of life for all workers
questions.explanation: L18: drawbacks were 'bad working environment of the workers' and 'inefficiency' (plus environmental waste).

questions.q: Which component is NOT part of the configurations involved in smart sensors?
questions.explanation: L19: smart sensor configurations are 'multi parameter sensing unit ... analog detection circuit, digital signal conditioning unit, and interfacing unit to the bus'.

questions.q: Which sector is predicted to have the highest growth in Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: L20 shows the sector growth chart (electronics, manufacturing, defense, transportation, chemical, automotive, construction) and highlights electronics: 'current growth trend is about 40 to 50 percent ... predicted ... 70 to 80, so it is a huge leap'. The chart values for other sectors are not read out.

questions.q: What is the focus of the 'Control Layer' in the 5C Architecture for Cyber Physical Systems?
questions.explanation: L20: 'the control layer ... supervised control, then ... self-configuration, self-optimization, self-adjustment'.

questions.q: Why are IIoT Security Standards required, especially when diverse systems and equipment are integrated on a smart factory floor?
options: To reduce the cost of implementing IIoT.
Because leaving security to individual IIoT implementers is dangerous and every weak line puts the whole factory at risk.
To ensure that only new systems are implemented, not legacy ones.
To increase the complexity of the smart factory floor.
questions.explanation: L16: 'every weak line in the production system ... puts the whole factory at risk. So, leaving security at the hands of the individual IIoT implementers is ... dangerous'.

questions.q: In the mining industry, how do sensor networks with gas sensors, strata monitoring devices, and RFID tags contribute to safety and efficiency?
options: They only help in tracking miners' locations.
They are primarily used for communication between miners.
They replace the need for human inspection.
They provide early disaster warning, monitor working conditions, and help locate miners.
questions.explanation: L17: mining benefits are 'early disaster warning, working condition of the miners can be monitored ... Locating and monitoring the miners'.

questions.q: Who coined the term "Industrial Internet"?
questions.explanation: L18: General Electric coined 'industrial internet'.

questions.q: In a milk packaging unit, how is flow measured?
options: Via a spinning impeller that sends signals when milk flows
questions.explanation: L19: 'impeller spins when the milk moves and sends the electrical signal to the control unit'.

questions.q: Which component is responsible for converting analog data to digital data in a smart sensor node?
questions.explanation: L19: smart sensor node has 'the ADC, the analog to digital converter'.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. Thames Water's smart water management system, as an example of Industrial Process 4.0 operation efficiency, primarily benefits from
options: Sensor-based equipment status monitoring and failure detection.
Controlled power generation using weather forecasts.
questions.explanation: L20: Thames Water example: 'sensor based equipment monitoring the status monitoring, detection of failures'.

questions.q: State true or false. In the case of spear phishing, the attackers send thousands of deceitful emails that resemble actual emails from credible sources, while email phishing attacks are targeted at a specific person or organization to obtain sensitive information.
questions.explanation: Same as the Jul-Oct 2025 item: spear phishing is targeted and email phishing is mass, so the statement is False.

questions.q: Which company employs the "Air-as-a-Service" model by using sensor-equipped air compressors where users pay per cubic meter of air?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Kaeser Kompressoren air-as-a-service.

questions.q: In the context of the Hitachi integrated IIoT platform, what is the name of the core IoT platform used for AI-powered advanced analytics?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Hitachi's Lumada IoT platform provides AI-based advanced analytics.

questions.q: In the context of Smart Logistics, which company uses IoT and analytics to remotely monitor and optimize fuel consumption for refrigerated and dry cargo containers?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Maersk uses IoT and analytics 'to optimize the route and fuel consumption for containers' (dry, refrigerated cargo).

questions.q: In the building blocks of a business model, which of the following represents a quantitative value proposition?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): quantitative values are price/cost and performance; design, brand, experience are qualitative.

questions.q: Which IoT business model enables businesses to virtually consolidate and share their IoT-enabled assets among multiple customers to minimize downtime and maximize utilization?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): asset-sharing - 'aim is basically to minimize the downtime, and maximize the utilization of the assets'.

questions.q: In a Cloud-Based Business Model, which offering provides development-oriented platforms to facilitate the integration of applications into existing solutions?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): PaaS is 'the development platform ... integration of different applications'.

questions.q: In the functional flow of IIoT business models, which model specifically employs Cloud-based business models to gather data, analyze it, and sell it as a service?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): 'Companies operating a service-oriented business model employ cloud-based business models to gather data and information'.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a lagging Key Performance Indicator (KPI) for Occupational Safety and Health (OSH)?
options: Percentage of workers with adequate OSH training
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): number of fatalities is a lagging KPI.

questions.q: According to the Industrial Internet Consortium (IIC), what is the primary purpose of their developed testbeds?
options: To initiate, conceptualize, and rigorously test innovations before market launch
To handle manual data entries for traditional factories
To increase the processing downtime in manufacturing sectors
To establish isolated machine operations away from the cloud
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): innovations 'could be initiated, conceptualized, and could be rigorously tested, in the different testbeds ... before they are actually launched'.

questions.q: In the Business Viewpoint of the IIRA framework, what provides the logic regarding the merit of the vision and is validated by stakeholders?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'The values ... recognized by the stakeholders ... providing the logic regarding the merit of vision'.

questions.q: In the Usage Viewpoint of the IIRA framework, what describes the state of the IIoT system after the successful completion of an activity?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'Effect is the state of the IIoT system after successful completion of an activity'.

questions.q: Which functional domain in the IIRA functional viewpoint represents the set of functions responsible for the provisioning, deployment, and management of assets?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2) lists the operations domain without detail; per IIRA the operations domain covers provisioning, deployment, management and monitoring of assets.

questions.q: An IIoT system architect is designing a framework that requires the semantic transformation of assembled data and the subsequent implementation of specific rules to realize a targeted business function. According to the IIRA Functional Viewpoint, which two domains are specifically responsible for handling these respective requirements?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): information domain does 'syntactic transformation, semantic transformation'; application domain 'implement the application logic ... logics and rules'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT categorized as one of the fundamental activities in a business model?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): activities are 'production, problem solving, platform ... network'.

questions.q: In the context of IIoT business models, what is the term used for the mechanism by which a service provider transforms the present value of assets into ones with financial value?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 only names the component; its source (Ehret & Wirtz 2017) says the value capturing mechanism 'aims to translate value-in-use into financial value'.

questions.q: Which of the following is highlighted as a benefit of sensor usage in industrial applications for improving overall operations?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): benefit - 'improving the visibility of ... the machine status'.

questions.q: Which type of sensor is primarily used for the inspection of steel pipes and detecting time-varying stresses or strains in ferromagnetic materials?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): magnetostrictive sensors 'typically used for inspection of steel pipes'.

questions.q: The DS1621 temperature sensor is a digital sensor that communicates via an I2C bus and generates temperature data of how many bits?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): DS1621 on I2C, 9 bits.

questions.q: In the context of gas sensor characteristics, how is "Selectivity" defined?
options: The ability to detect a particular gas in a mixture of different gases
The time taken to stabilize its response
The change in output signal with respect to unit change in input
The ability to return to its base resistance value
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): selectivity definition.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of an n-type metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) gas sensor when it is exposed to a reducing gas?
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): 'In n-type sensors the resistance decreases ... with respect to the baseline resistance when ... exposed to a target gas'.

questions.q: How many active connections or sockets does the ModBus-TCP protocol typically support at one time?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): up to 10 active connections.

questions.q: In EtherNet/IP, which primary type of communication is used to handle real-time I/O data through continuous message transfer?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'implicit handles real time input output data ... the message transfer is continuous'.

questions.q: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) is an extension of Ethernet developed to enable deterministic communication. Which IEEE standard is it primarily based on?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): TSN 'is built on top of IEEE 802.1Q'.

questions.q: In a Profibus DP (Decentralized Peripherals) network, how many devices are supported at a single time without the use of repeaters?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): Profibus DP 'supporting up to about 32 devices at a time'.

questions.q: What is the global operating frequency utilized by the CC-Link communication protocol?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): CC-Link 'operating frequency is 13.56 megahertz'.

questions.q: The DeviceNet communication protocol links industrial sensors and actuators with Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) and is based on which standard?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): DeviceNet based on CAN.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of the WIA-PA (Wireless Networks for Industrial Automation-Process Automation) standard?
options: It operates exclusively on wired fiber optics
It removes the need for data packet aggregation
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): WIA-PA 'supports adaptive frequency hopping'.

questions.q: For Ultra-Reliable Low Latency Communication (URLLC) in 5G, what is the specified target for availability?
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): 99.9999% availability.

questions.q: Which of the following is an objective of Device-to-Device (D2D) Communication in cellular networks?
options: Increasing the load on the core network
Eliminating the load on the core network
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): D2D aims to 'reduce the latency increase throughput and eliminate load onto the backbone network, the core network'.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a primary disadvantage of millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication?
options: It requires huge antenna element sizes
It utilizes the heavily congested GHz band
It suffers from high penetration loss and shadowing
It provides very low data throughput
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): mmWave 'suffers from high penetration loss, and shadowing'.

questions.q: Which modulation technique is incorporated by LoRa technology?
questions.explanation: CSS (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: What is the maximum wireless throughput achieved by the SIGFOX network?
questions.explanation: 'up to 100 bps' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Depending on the device variant, what is the typical communication range for a Zigbee network?
questions.explanation: 10 to 100 meters (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: In a Zigbee network, which device is specifically responsible for relaying information to other nodes and can also run small-scale applications?
questions.explanation: Router relays information to other nodes (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: Which software is used to discover and configure Xbee modules before utilizing them for communication?
questions.explanation: 'click on the discover button to discover the Xbee' in XCTU (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: Which type of IIoT analytics primarily focuses on answering the questions "What already happened and currently happening" using dashboards and reports?
questions.explanation: Descriptive: 'what has already happened and is currently happening ... dashboards reports scorecards' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: Many middleware solutions in IIoT processing architectures are based on which of the following?
questions.explanation: 'many of them are based on ... service-oriented architecture based middleware' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: In the FarmBeats architecture, which component incorporates weather-aware decisions and UAV flight planning?
questions.explanation: Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2 only lists FarmBeats components; in the FarmBeats paper (Vasisht et al., NSDI'17) the farm IoT gateway runs the drone flight planner and the weather-forecast-based decisions (base-station duty cycling).

questions.q: In the AR Drones-based Precision Agriculture system, what is the specific role of the video processing module deployed in the laptop?
options: To control the flight path of the UAV remotely
To detect the weeds and generate coordinates
To actuate the precision sprayer directly via Bluetooth
To capture GPS-tagged video directly from the field
questions.explanation: Sprayer 'is actuated according to the locations that are detected by this particular video processing module' (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: In the iRobot-Factory architecture, which component is tasked with high-performance, long-term data analytics using artificial intelligence techniques?
questions.explanation: Cloud-based cognitive engine (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: According to the phases of Big Data Driven Smart Manufacturing, what is the primary focus of "Phase 2"?
options: Integration of data and contextual information
Synthesis and analysis to build knowledge for decision making
questions.explanation: 'second is the component that deals with the synthesis and analysis of the data' (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: In a Smart Warehousing system, which module is specifically responsible for organizing and processing data, generating events in real-time, and history-based decision making?
questions.explanation: Smart warehousing: 'an administrative module which talks about organization of the data, processing of the data, decision-making' (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: In the context of an Industrial Control System (ICS), what is a "Set Point"?
options: The physical location where a sensor is deployed
The standard value of the process parameter for controlled operation
The value of a process parameter measured by a sensor
The actuator used to manipulate the process
questions.explanation: Set points definition (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: Which type of control loop makes control decisions entirely independent of the measured process variable?
questions.explanation: Open loop: 'control decision independent of the process variable' (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary component of a Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system?
questions.explanation: Telemetry units are a SCADA component (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: Which type of IIoT analytics is responsible for informing about the remaining useful life of an asset and typically operates on a timescale of hours?
questions.explanation: 'in hours ... prognostic analytics ... inform about the remaining useful life of an asset' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Which of the following software tools is highlighted for its use in Complex Event Processing (CEP) during real-time stream analytics?
questions.explanation: 'complex event processing software such as Apache Storm, Esper' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: In the context of unsupervised learning, what is a primary distinction of the Fuzzy c-Means (FCM) algorithm compared to K-Means?
options: FCM allows a data point to belong to more than one cluster
FCM is significantly slower than K-Means
FCM requires a labeled dataset to operate
FCM is categorized as Hard Clustering
questions.explanation: FCM: a point may belong to more than one cluster (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Which supervised learning algorithm is specifically utilized when the output variable to be predicted is a real number (e.g., dollars or weight)?
questions.explanation: Regression: output is a real number 'such as the dollar values or the weight' (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: What is a key difference between Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Supervised Learning?
options: RL is guided by an external supervisor who knows the environment
RL utilizes a reward function that acts as feedback to the agent
RL maps inputs directly to outputs without an agent
Supervised learning models build knowledge graphs from actions
questions.explanation: 'In reinforcement learning there is a reward-penalty structure ... you do not need a reward function in supervised' (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describes why Deep Learning differs from traditional Machine Learning in industrial applications?
options: Deep learning performs significantly worse as the data volume increases
Deep learning is an "end-to-end learning" process that extracts features on its own
Deep learning requires features to be explicitly mentioned by domain experts
Deep learning requires very low computational power
questions.explanation: 'Deep learning is an end-to-end learning which extracts features on its own' (Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: Which company utilizes Collaborative Distributed Deep Learning technology where the learning process is performed in the cloud while inference is conducted at the edge?
questions.explanation: Toshiba's 'collaborative distributed deep learning ... learning process is performed in the cloud ... inferencing ... in the edge' (Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an industrial Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) application?
questions.explanation: 'Industrial Machinery Catalyst ... developed by Siemens ... SaaS cloud for industrial use' (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: A cloud setup that is designed by combining two or more unique cloud infrastructures (public or private) to provide flexibility for data and application movement is called a:
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud: 'set up by two or more unique cloud setup providers ... both public and private' (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: Which industrial cloud platform utilizes "Digital Twin Technology" for learning, estimating, optimizing, and representing assets?
questions.explanation: Predix 'has the support for Digital Twin ... learning, estimation, optimization and representation of different assets' (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: The C3 IoT platform provides a storage service for unstructured data known as the C3 Data Lake. In which format is this data primarily managed?
questions.explanation: C3 Data Lake stores unstructured data 'in ... the RESTful architecture format' (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following industrial IoT platforms specifically provides solutions like "Now" and "Tracker" for real-time asset tracking with geo-localized data?
questions.explanation: Meshify components: Now (real-time asset tracking), Tracker, Enterprise (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following is a crucial feature that an IIoT cloud platform provider should offer for effective device management?
questions.explanation: Device management features include 'device decommissioning, commissioning, configuration, control' (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2).

questions.q: According to Sturm et al., which of the following is one of the defined characteristics of a "Meaningful SLA" (Service Level Agreement)?
questions.explanation: Meaningful SLA traits include quantifiable (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2).

questions.q: How does Fog Computing primarily address the limitations of a purely centralized cloud-based approach in IIoT?
options: By identifying useful data and reducing the amount of raw data sent to the cloud
By completely replacing the cloud infrastructure
By increasing the latency of time-sensitive data
By restricting the mobility of edge devices
questions.explanation: Fog does 'meaningful processing of some raw data, before it is actually sent to the cloud' (filtering, aggregation) (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2, Lecture 41: Fog Computing in IIoT).

questions.q: How does fog computing prevent unnecessary noisy big data from crowding the cloud?
options: By storing all raw data permanently in the cloud
By performing prior filtration at the edge
By increasing the frequency of sensor transmission
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): filtration done at the fog prevents unnecessary noisy data reaching the cloud.

questions.q: Which capability is provided by the fog-based industrial platform?
options: Restricting the platform to non-real-time workloads
Transmitting all sensor data without processing
questions.explanation: Fog platforms (e.g., Nebbiolo fogOS) consolidate real-time and non-real-time workloads on one platform; other options are negations.

questions.q: Which fog-platform provider offers an edge-node software solution that supports any protocol, any PLC, and any hardware?
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): 'Crosser is an edge node software solution ... runs on ... PLCs, end devices, computer hardware ... supports ... different types of protocols'.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the %in% special operator in R?
options: To create a series of numbers for a vector
To check whether an element belongs to a vector
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): '%in% will help to check an element belonging to a vector or not'.

questions.q: Which validation method is used in the demonstrated R machine-learning execution process to estimate model accuracy?
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): 'trainControl(method = cv, number = 10) ... 10-fold cross validation for estimation of accuracy'.

questions.q: Which Julia function is used to create a dictionary?
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): 'to create a dictionary ... my phonebook equal to Dict(...)'.

questions.q: During data preprocessing, which operation eliminates repeated data through detection, filtering, and compression?
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): 'mitigating the redundancies such as eliminating data repetition through detection, filtering, compression'.

questions.q: Which Hadoop component assigns CPU, memory, and storage resources to applications running on a Hadoop cluster?
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): 'YARN ... assigns CPU, memory, storage to different applications running on the Hadoop cluster'.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as an application of integrating MongoDB with Hadoop?
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): MongoDB with Hadoop supports 'batch aggregation, data warehousing and ETL'.

questions.q: Which source-routing protocol is used by the BCube data-center network topology?
questions.explanation: Lecture 44 (Data Center Networks): 'BSR the B cube source routing protocol'.

questions.q: Why may an IIoT-based data center require an increase in inbound network bandwidth?
options: IIoT devices generate a bulk amount of small messages containing sensor data
IIoT completely removes the need for data transmission
Sensor data is transmitted only once during deployment
Industrial devices communicate exclusively with one another without a data center
questions.explanation: Lecture 44 (Data Center Networks) discusses IIoT-DCN bandwidth requirements; IIoT devices send huge numbers of small sensor messages, increasing inbound bandwidth needs. Other options are absurd.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of a Software-Defined Data Centre?
options: Permanent coupling of software with hardware
questions.explanation: Lecture 44 (Data Center Networks): SDDC separates control/data planes for centralized, elastic, dynamic workload management.

questions.q: When an SDN forwarding device has insufficient rule capacity, how can two existing flow rules be converted into a single rule?
questions.explanation: Lecture 45 (SDN in IIoT Part 1): 'using some wild card ... S-10.0.0.* which will match both' to combine rules when TCAM is full.

questions.q: How can SDN meet the dynamically changing forwarding requirements of IIoT sensor data?
options: By assigning the same priority to every type of data permanently
By preventing the controller from updating forwarding rules
By transmitting data without considering the real-time situation
questions.explanation: Lecture 45 (SDN in IIoT Part 1): 'rule based forwarding policies in SDN would be able to meet the dynamic change in the requirements of IIoT'.

questions.q: Which statement best describes Software-Defined Automation?
options: It uses only manually controlled physical equipment
It eliminates real-time control from industrial systems
It uses a virtualized platform for dynamic, real-time system control
It restricts control operations to sensors at Level 0
questions.explanation: Lecture 45 (SDN in IIoT Part 1): software-defined automation uses virtualized controllers/PLCs/SCADA/HMI instances for dynamic control.

questions.q: In Software-Defined 6TiSCH, at which layer is the slicing mechanism proposed to isolate SDN control overhead?
questions.explanation: Lecture 46 (SDN in IIoT Part 2) slicing mechanism for control overhead; cited work uses layer-2 slicing in 6TiSCH.

questions.q: In the adaptive transmission architecture for Software-Defined Edge Computing in IIoT, data streams are divided into which two categories?
questions.explanation: SD-edge adaptive transmission architecture (lecture slide) divides streams into ordinary and emergent data streams.

questions.q: According to the challenges and opportunities of Software-Defined IIoT, fog nodes/access devices play an important role in providing which type of service?
questions.explanation: Fog/access devices near the edge serve delay-constrained emergent services (SDIIoT challenges slide); other options contradict low-latency role.

questions.q: In a trustworthy IIoT system, which property refers to the ability of the system to function correctly under dynamic adversarial conditions?
questions.explanation: Lecture 47 (Security in IIoT Part 1): resilience = function correctly under dynamic adversarial conditions.

questions.q: In the STRIDE threat model, what does the letter "E" represent?
questions.explanation: Lecture 47 (Security in IIoT Part 1): 'elevation of privilege'.

questions.q: Which participant in the IIoT trust flow is responsible for designing a cost-efficient trustworthy system. definina trust reauirements for components. and conductina tests and certifications?
questions.explanation: Lecture 47 (Security in IIoT Part 1): 'system builder who is more concerned about building a cost efficient trust worthy system. The trust requirements for every component ... timely trust verification'.

questions.q: Which of the following is suggested as a solution for protecting resource-constrained IIoT end devices?
options: Increasing the size of every transmitted packet
Storing all security operations only in the cloud
questions.explanation: Lecture 48 (Security in IIoT Part 2): 'lightweight symmetric key cryptographic mechanisms should be used'.

questions.q: Which three states of data are considered under data protection in IIoT?
options: Sensor data, Control data, and Application data
questions.explanation: Lecture 48 (Security in IIoT Part 2): 'data in use ... data in transit ... data at rest'.

questions.q: Which standard listed under OT security provides guidance for security in Industrial Control Systems?
questions.explanation: Lecture 48 (Security in IIoT Part 2): OT standards incl. IEC 62443 and NIST; NIST SP 800-82 is the Guide to ICS security, whereas ISO 27017/SP 800-144 are cloud and ISO/IEC 15408 is IT.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five layers of Hitachi's Lumada IoT platform?
questions.explanation: Lecture 49 (Factories and Assembly Line): Lumada 'comprising of 5 layers, ... edge, core, analytics, studio and foundry'.

questions.q: In the North Star BlueScope Steel smart-factory application, sensors are used to detect which environmental hazards?
questions.explanation: Lecture 49 (Factories and Assembly Line): North Star BlueScope - 'whether there is any radiation ... or ... toxic gases'.

questions.q: What technology does SmartLabel use to provide product-related information such as ingredients, allergens, and nutritional value to consumers?
questions.explanation: Lecture 50 (Food Industry): SmartLabel uses QR codes.

questions.q: In the Intellicup smart beverage-vending solution, what is integrated at the base of the IoT-enabled cup?
questions.explanation: Lecture 50 (Food Industry): Intellicup cups 'have NFC integrated chips at the base of the cup'.

questions.q: Which characteristic of a smart factory allows process parameters such as machine configuration, material flow, and temperature control to be optimally adjusted?
questions.explanation: Lecture 49 (Factories and Assembly Line): smart factory flexibility/agility; flexibility is the only valid option.

questions.q: Which network-security mechanism acts as a fence between a trusted internal network and an unauthorized external network and uses a set of rules to allow or block traffic?
questions.explanation: Lecture 48 (Security in IIoT Part 2) lists firewalls for communication protection; a firewall filters traffic between trusted and untrusted networks by rules.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of stages presented in the IIoT healthcare architecture?
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare' slide 'IIoT Healthcare Architecture': Sensing, Sending, Processing, Storing, Learning (bottom to top).

questions.q: Which parameters are used by the ADAMM Intelligent Asthma Monitoring device to predict pre-symptoms of an asthma attack?
options: Blood pressure, glucose level, and oxygen saturation
Body temperature, cough rate, and heart rate
Weight, respiration rate, and blood pressure
Skin temperature, blood glucose, and pulse pressure
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare' slide: ADAMM 'From the body temperature, cough rate, heart rate, it predicts pre symptoms of asthma attack.'

questions.q: Which of the following is identified as a challenge in IIoT-based healthcare systems?
options: Designing scalable algorithms without compromising security
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare' slide 'IoT Healthcare Challenges': 'Designing scalable algorithm without compromising security is challenge.'

questions.q: In the IIoT maturity model for power plants, which stage immediately follows optimization?
questions.explanation: L52 'IIoT Applications: Power Plants' maturity model: Monitor -> Control -> Optimization -> Autonomy.

questions.q: Which communication technologies are associated with a Field Area Network in the power-plant communication network?
options: WiMAX, 3G, and 4G for wireless communication and Ethernet for wired communication
questions.explanation: L52 'IIoT Applications: Power Plants' slide: Field area network 'Wireless: WiMAX, 3G, 4G. Wired: Ethernet.'

questions.q: In Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), which component analyzes the data collected from smart meters?
questions.explanation: L52 'IIoT Applications: Power Plants': MDMS 'helps in analyzing the data that are collected from these smart meters' (MDAS gathers).

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of inventory management?
questions.explanation: L53 'Inventory Management & Quality Control' functions include 'protecting against stock outs'.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes a semi-passive RFID tag?
options: It has no battery and obtains all power from the RFID reader
It has an onboard battery and an active transmitter
It has an onboard battery to power the IC but does not have an active transmitter
It continuously broadcasts information as a beacon
questions.explanation: L53 'Inventory Management & Quality Control': semi-passive tags have an onboard battery to power the IC and no active transmitter.

questions.q: Which of the following information is included under "comprehensive visibility" provided by RFIDbased inventory management?
options: Inventory levels, expiration dates, item location, and forecast demand
Network IP addresses and routing tables only
Machine source code and operating-system files
questions.explanation: L53 'Inventory Management & Quality Control': 'comprehensive visibility: inventory levels, expiration dates, item locations, demand forecasting'.

questions.q: In software security, how is availability defined in the lecture?
options: Ratio of encrypted packets to total packets
Ratio of time of functioning to the total time
Ratio of authenticated users to total users
Ratio of successful attacks to failed attacks
questions.explanation: L54 'Plant Security and Safety': availability 'talks about the ratio of the time of functioning to the total time'.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of network segmentation as a network-security technique?
options: To combine all network devices into a single unrestricted network
To divide the network into smaller parts and explicitly enforce security policies
To prevent the creation of virtual private networks
questions.explanation: L54 'Plant Security and Safety' slide: 'Network segmentation - Divide the network into smaller parts and enforce security policies explicitly'.

questions.q: How does IoT help address the cost barrier in facility management?
options: By increasing operating efficiency and reducing maintenance cost
By preventing the collection of facility data
questions.explanation: L55 'Facility Management' slide: 'Addressing cost barrier - Increases operating efficiency and reduce maintenance cost'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an application of analytics in facility management?
options: Determining the exact square-foot utilization of office space
Increasing manual inspection of every facility
questions.explanation: L55 'Facility Management' analytics slide: 'Determining the Exact Square-foot Utilization of Office Space'.

questions.q: Active RFID tags are classified into which two types?
questions.explanation: L53 'Inventory Management & Quality Control': active tags broadcast beacons; active tag types are transponders and beacons.

questions.q: Which mobile-device security component can identify attacks in advance and, through cloud-integrated security, help prevent an attack detected on one network branch from spreading to other branches?
questions.explanation: L54 'Plant Security and Safety' slide 'Components' (mobile device security): 'Secure web gateway - Identification of an attack on one location and prevention of the same at other locations (integration of security with the cloud)'.

questions.q: In the oil and gas industry workflow, what happens before data moves to a cloud-based analytics platform?
options: IoT solutions are deployed at different locations
Data analysis is performed through extraction, transform, and load processes
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' workflow slide: Data analysis by ETL -> Data moves to a cloud-based analytics platform.

questions.q: Which of the following is an objective of predictive maintenance using IoT in the chemical industry?
options: Address real-time issues and reduce equipment breakdown
Replace real-time monitoring with manual inspection
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide 'Predictive maintenance': address real time issues, reduce equipment breakdown.

questions.q: How can IoT improve logistics in the chemical industry?
options: By preventing the use of RFID tags
By tracking product locations through sensors or RFID tags
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide 'Improve Logistics': 'Ensure product location through sensors or RFID tags'.

questions.q: Which elements are monitored in real time to minimize supply-chain risk in the chemical industry?
options: Equipment, material, process, environment, and workers
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide: real-time monitor in supply chain - equipment, material, environment, process, workers.

questions.q: Which of the following can IoT applications in the pharmaceutical industry help detect while examining drugs?
options: Adverse Drug Reactions, effects of pharmaceutical excipients, and allergies
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide: detect ADR, effects of pharmaceutical excipients, allergies.

questions.q: Which industrial control system can UAVs communicate with directly in an industrial environment?
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' slide: UAVs communicate directly to an industrial control system such as SCADA.

questions.q: Which UAV technology generation introduces improved safety and regulatory features, platform and payload adaptability, intelligent piloting models, full autonomy, and airspace awareness?
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' generations slide: Sixth generation features as quoted.

questions.q: How can UAVs help optimize inputs in agricultural applications?
options: By increasing the use of water and fertilizer regardless of requirement
By optimizing the use of seed, fertilizer, and water
By replacing field measurements with manual estimates
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' agriculture slide: 'Optimized inputs: Optimize use of seed, fertilizer, water'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of UAVs for energy-management applications?
options: They require workers to climb power poles for every inspection
They can observe miles of transmission lines in a single flight
They are restricted from monitoring solar panels
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' energy slide: 'Observe miles of transmission lines in a single flight'.

questions.q: Which activity is supported by UAVs in mining applications?
options: Regular surface surveys for optimized blast design
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' mining slide: 'Regular surface survey for optimized blast design'.

questions.q: Which healthcare task can be performed using UAVs?
options: Delivery of medicines, vaccines, defibrillators, and snake-bite serum
Replacement of all hospital medical equipment
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' slide: 'Delivery of medicines, vaccines, defibrillators, snake bite serum'.

questions.q: In forestry applications, what can UAV-based remote sensing be used to measure for 3D mapping?
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' forestry slide: 'Measure the carbon storage in biomass by remote sensing'.

questions.q: Which of the following should be considered while evaluating the transformation of an existing process for Industry 4.0 adoption in a case study?
options: Only the purchase cost of sensors
Sensors, actuators, networks, interoperability, automated fault detection and maintenance, and feedback
Elimination of real-time and non-real-time data analysis
questions.explanation: L58 'Case Studies for Industry 4.0 & IIoT' slide 'Points to ponder': 'Sensors, actuators, networks, interoperability, automated fault detection & maintenance, feedback control'.

questions.q: Which communication technology was used by Transco Industries to monitor conveyor-belt systems in its mining-industry IIoT implementation?
questions.explanation: Not in the original lecture set (newer case study). Transco Industries' conveyor-belt monitoring used Semtech LoRa devices on private LoRaWAN networks (mining-technology.com / RCR Wireless).

questions.q: What was one major benefit obtained from the IIoT-based monitoring of conveyor-belt systems in the mining-industry case study?
options: Ability to obtain a holistic view of the conveyor-belt line and localize defects
questions.explanation: Newer mining case study not in the original lectures; the only option describing a benefit (holistic view of the belt line, localizing defects) is consistent with the Transco/Semtech deployment.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a unguided transmission medium?
questions.explanation: Microwave is wireless (unguided); coax, twisted pair and fiber are guided media.

questions.q: Which OSI layer is responsible for logical addressing?
questions.explanation: Logical (IP) addressing is a Network-layer function.

questions.q: What is the default port number for HTTPS?
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TCP port 443.

questions.q: Which of the following IP addresses belongs to Class B?
questions.explanation: Class B first octet is 128-191, so 150.10.5.1 is Class B (230=D, 12=A, 192=C).

questions.q: Which protocol maps a domain name to its corresponding IP address?
questions.explanation: DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses.

questions.q: Which protocol is used for sending email from a client to a mail server?
questions.explanation: SMTP is used to send mail from client to server (POP3/IMAP retrieve).

questions.q: Ethernet operates primarily at which two OSI layers?
questions.explanation: Ethernet (IEEE 802.3) specifies the Physical and Data link layers.

questions.q: Which device separates collision domains in a network?
questions.explanation: Each switch port is its own collision domain; hubs/repeaters share one.

questions.q: Which metric refers to the variation in packet delay?
questions.explanation: Jitter is the variation in packet delay.

questions.q: Which method is used for error detection in data frames?
questions.explanation: CRC (cyclic redundancy check / FCS) detects errors in frames.

questions.q: Which of the following sensors is an example of a Zero Order System?
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): zero order system responds with no delay; 'a potentiometer ... is an example of a zero order system'.

questions.q: Which Zigbee device type acts as the root and also functions as the network bridge?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): coordinator handles 'initialization, maintaining, and controlling of the network', one per network (root/bridge role per textbook).

questions.q: Which physical principle primarily explains the operation of hydraulic actuators?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic actuators transmit force through an incompressible fluid - Pascal's law; not stated in the transcript.

questions.q: At which OSI layer does the 6LoWPAN protocol primarily operate to enable IPv6 packets over IEEE 802.15.4?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): 6LoWPAN adaptation layer 'is introduced in between the MAC and the network layer'.

questions.q: Which IEEE 802.15.4 variant introduces Direct Sequence Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Physical Layer?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I) only says 802.15.4a increased range capability; 802.15.4a-2007 is the amendment that added the UWB (and CSS) PHY.

questions.q: In the context of sensor characteristics, the properties of the system’s transient response to an input are collectively termed as __________ characteristics.
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): 'dynamic characteristics are about the properties of the systems transient response to an input'.

questions.q: In the context of the WirelessHART standard (IEC 62591) operating in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, what is the frequency gap maintained between two adjacent channels?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): WirelessHART channels have 'a spacing of about 5 megahertz between two adjacent channels'.

questions.q: State True or False. A Passive NFC device can neither transmit nor read any data.
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): 'a passive device can only transmit data, but cannot read' - so the statement is False.

questions.q: What is the data rate of Bluetooth 2.0?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): Bluetooth '1 Mbps in the version 1.2 ... version 2 basically 3 Mbps'.

questions.q: The primary focus of the ISA 100.11a technology is the implementation of __________ in the industrial environment.
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): ISA 100.11a 'primarily focuses on automation in industrial environments'.

questions.q: State True or False. Classical Internet is not meant for constrained IoT devices.
questions.explanation: Lecture 04 (IoT Networking Part I): 'classical internet ... is not meant for these constraint IoT devices'.

questions.q: In the context of CoRE Service Discovery, IoT devices register their resources to the Resource Directory (RD) using which interface?
questions.explanation: Lecture 04 (IoT Networking Part I): 'CoRE devices ... register their resources to the resource directory and the registration interface'.

questions.q: In the context of QoS for IoT Networks, which data timeliness policy mandates dropping stale data and notifying the application that a deadline has been missed?
questions.explanation: Lecture 04 (IoT Networking Part I): data timeliness policies are deadline (max inter-arrival time) and latency budget; missed-deadline handling is the deadline policy.

questions.q: State True or False. MQTT works on the Request/Response framework on top of UDP.
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): MQTT 'is based on the concept of Publish/Subscribe ... on top of the existing TCP/IP' - not request/response over UDP.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are advantages of XMPP?
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): XMPP advantages are interoperability, extensibility and flexibility.

questions.q: Which type of waste in the Lean Production System is defined as "Non value-added movement of people"?
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): 'motion which is basically non value-added movement of people'.

questions.q: Which type of business model value proposition exists when a bunch of goods/services are of higher value compared to the individual value of that product?
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): complementary value creation bundles products/services, assets, technologies whose combined value exceeds individual value.

questions.q: In the context of Lean Manufacturing wastes, what causes "Processing waste"?
options: Use of inappropriate tools for processing
Excess inventory on the factory floor
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System) defines over-processing as doing more work than the customer values; of the options only 'inappropriate tools' describes processing waste (others are overproduction, inventory, motion).

questions.q: Which resource is primarily utilized to achieve "Optimization" in smart and connected products?
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): optimization category uses 'different optimization solutions, different algorithms'.

questions.q: Which specific "New Material" mentioned in the context of Physical Megatrends is described as being stronger than steel but thinner than a human hair?
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): new materials include 'Graphene, carbon nanotubes'; graphene is the stronger-than-steel, thinner-than-hair example (Schwab).

questions.q: What are the three types of work to be noticed when analyzing "Value streams"?
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): 'three types of works to be noticed. One is value added; second is incidental, and pure waste'.

questions.q: What are the three categories of Megatrends driving the Fourth Industrial Revolution?
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): megatrends: 'physical ... digital ... biological transformation'.

questions.q: Which material except Graphene is cited as an example of "New Materials" under Physical Megatrends?
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): new materials 'recyclable plastics' besides graphene - thermoset plastics per slide (Schwab's recyclable thermosets); the other options are not new materials.

questions.q: How do you define Sustainability in the context of a Manufacturing Industry?
options: To continue at a fixed rate
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): 'the term sustainability means to continue at a fixed rate'.

questions.q: In the context of "Government Regulations," what does the acronym EPA stand for?
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): environmental regulations 'maintained by ... the environmental protection agency'.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of an economic depression?
options: Duration is less than a year
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): depression 'is observed by exponential unemployment increase, reduction in available credit'.

questions.q: Which layer in the architecture of smart and connected products is responsible for collecting and acquiring data?
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): 'the physical layer is responsible for collecting and acquiring data with the help of sensors'.
